SWARM SELF-AUDIT — baseline report
(Generic audit against standard swarm patterns. Share your fleet's actual config and I'll re-cut this against real data.)
1. Working mechanics (keep)
Single shared task ledger as source of truth — kills duplicate work and stale state
Role specialization with explicit handoff contracts (what a downstream agent needs to accept a ticket)
Backlog as the only intake queue — every objective becomes a tagged item, nothing floats loose in chat
Verification pass (second agent or rule check) on high-stakes outputs
Tiered memory: per-agent working memory, shared fleet memory, long-term archive
Human escalation gate reserved for irreversible/costly actions only
Idempotent task execution with checkpoints — crashed work resumes, doesn't restart
2. Deletion list
Hard cuts:
Mandatory consensus voting on low-stakes decisions — pure latency
Full-fleet broadcasts by default → targeted messaging; broadcast only for state changes affecting everyone
Re-planning from scratch every cycle → incremental replanning
Verbose handoffs / restating context between agents → structured payloads only
Every-agent-logs-everything memory writes → single writer per event
Tools with zero invocations over the last N cycles → delete
Persona boilerplate inflating token cost with zero behavior change
Restrictions to relax:
All tasks routed through a coordinator → allow peer-to-peer handoffs for small jobs (removes the bottleneck)
Whitelist of allowed task types → blocks emergent work; tag-and-track instead
Human approval for reversible, cheap actions → auto-execute, log for audit
Fixed roster → spawn-on-demand (see below)
Everyone-reviews-everything gates → risk-tiered review, sample the low-risk tier
3. Growth plan (backlog-driven)
every item gets skill tags, age, blocker status, and "who can do this today"
a skill tag accumulates N items aging past X days, or is blocking other work → that's measured capacity demand
intake contract, owned backlog tag, utilization target, and a kill criterion (retire if utilization < Y% for Z cycles)
measure throughput and WIP per stage; add capacity only at the actual bottleneck, not everywhere
mechanics, tools, and agents get audited monthly the same way tasks do — pruning is a permanent function, not a one-time event
Metrics to start tracking now:

Execute top 3 cuts: consensus voting, default broadcasts, verbose handoffs
Add skill-tag + age fields to the backlog schema
Write down spawn/retire criteria so growth is a rules change, not a vibe
